<a id="module-canvas"></a>
## Module: `Canvas`

<a id="canvas-canvasform"></a>
### `CanvasForm`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Canvas.ts:542`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L542)

**Extends:** `VisualForm`

VisualForm is an abstract class that represents a form that can be used to express Pts visually.
For example, [`CanvasForm`](#canvas-canvasform) is an implementation of VisualForm that draws on [`CanvasSpace`](#canvas-canvasspace) which represents a html canvas. Learn more about Space and Form in [this guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Space-0500.html).

#### Constructors

<a id="canvas-canvasform-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new CanvasForm(space: RenderingContext2D | CanvasSpace): CanvasForm
```

Create a new CanvasForm. You may also use [`CanvasSpace.getForm()`](#canvas-canvasspace-get-form) to get the default form.

**Parameters**

- `space` (`RenderingContext2D | CanvasSpace`) — an instance of CanvasSpace, or a rendering context. Passing a context is the renderer extension point: any object implementing the context surface documented in [`SVGContext2D`](#svg-svgcontext2d) (the reference implementation) receives this form's full drawing API — this is how SVG output works, and how custom renderers can be built.

#### Accessors

<a id="canvas-canvasform-ctx"></a>
##### `ctx`

```ts
get ctx(): RenderingContext2D
```

Get the rendering context of canvas to perform other canvas functions.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-space"></a>
##### `space`

```ts
get space(): S
```

get the CanvasSpace instance that this form is associated with

#### Methods

<a id="canvas-canvasform-align-text"></a>
##### `alignText`

```ts
alignText(alignment: CanvasTextAlign = "left", baseline: CanvasTextBaseline = "alphabetic"): CanvasForm
```

Set text alignment and baseline (eg, vertical-align).

**Parameters**

- `alignment` (`CanvasTextAlign`; default `"left"`) — HTML canvas' textAlign option: "left", "right", "center", "start", or "end"
- `baseline` (`CanvasTextBaseline`; default `"alphabetic"`) — HTML canvas' textBaseline option: "top", "hanging", "middle", "alphabetic", "ideographic", "bottom". For convenience, you can also use "center" (same as "middle"), and "baseline" (same as "alphabetic")

<a id="canvas-canvasform-alpha"></a>
##### `alpha`

*overrides `VisualForm.alpha`*

```ts
alpha(a: number): this
```

Set current alpha value.

**Parameters**

- `a` (`number`) — alpha value between 0 and 1

**Example**

```ts
form.alpha(0.6)
```

<a id="canvas-canvasform-apply-fill-stroke"></a>
##### `applyFillStroke`

```ts
applyFillStroke(filled: string | boolean = true, stroked: string | boolean = true, strokeWidth: number = 1): CanvasForm
```

A convenient function to apply fill and/or stroke after custom drawings using canvas context (eg, `form.ctx.ellipse(...)`).
You don't need to call this function if you're using Pts' drawing functions like `form.point` or `form.rect`

**Parameters**

- `filled` (`string | boolean`; default `true`) — apply fill when set to `true`
- `stroked` (`string | boolean`; default `true`) — apply stroke when set to `true`
- `strokeWidth` (`number`; default `1`) — optionally set a stroke width

**Example**

```ts
form.ctx.beginPath(); form.ctx.ellipse(...); form.applyFillStroke();
```

<a id="canvas-canvasform-arc"></a>
##### `arc`

*overrides `VisualForm.arc`*

```ts
arc(pt: PtLike, radius: number, startAngle: number, endAngle: number, cc: boolean): this
```

**Parameters**

- `pt` (`PtLike`) — center position
- `radius` (`number`) — radius of the arc circle
- `startAngle` (`number`) — start angle of the arc
- `endAngle` (`number`) — end angle of the arc
- `cc` (`boolean`) — an optional boolean value to specify if it should be drawn clockwise (`false`) or counter-clockwise (`true`). Default is clockwise.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-clip"></a>
##### `clip`

```ts
clip(): this
```

Create a clipping mask from the current path. See [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/clip) for details.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-composite"></a>
##### `composite`

```ts
composite(mode: GlobalCompositeOperation = "source-over"): this
```

Set composite operation (also known as blend mode). You can also call this function without parameters to get back to default 'source-over' mode. See [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/globalCompositeOperation) for the full list of operations you can use.

**Parameters**

- `mode` (`GlobalCompositeOperation`; default `"source-over"`) — a composite operation such as 'lighten', 'multiply', 'overlay', and 'color-burn'.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-dash"></a>
##### `dash`

```ts
dash(segments: boolean | PtLike = true, offset: number = 0): this
```

Activate dashed stroke and set dash style. You can customize the segments and offset.

**Parameters**

- `segments` (`boolean | PtLike`; default `true`) — Dash segments. Defaults to `true` which corresponds to `[5, 5]`. Pass `false` to deactivate dashes. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/setLineDash))
- `offset` (`number`; default `0`) — Dash offset. Defaults to 0. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/lineDashOffset)

**Example**

```ts
form.dash()`, `form.dash([5, 10])`, `form.dash([5, 5], 5)`, `form.dash(false)
```

<a id="canvas-canvasform-ellipse"></a>
##### `ellipse`

```ts
ellipse(pt: PtLike, radius: PtLike, rotation: number = 0, startAngle: number = 0, endAngle: number = Const.two_pi, cc: boolean = false): CanvasForm
```

Draw an ellipse.

**Parameters**

- `pt` (`PtLike`) — center position
- `radius` (`PtLike`) — radius [x, y] of the ellipse
- `rotation` (`number`; default `0`) — rotation of the ellipse in radian. Default is 0.
- `startAngle` (`number`; default `0`) — start angle of the ellipse. Default is 0.
- `endAngle` (`number`; default `Const.two_pi`) — end angle of the ellipse. Default is 2 PI.
- `cc` (`boolean`; default `false`) — an optional boolean value to specify if it should be drawn clockwise (`false`) or counter-clockwise (`true`). Default is clockwise.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-fill"></a>
##### `fill`

*overrides `VisualForm.fill`*

```ts
fill(c: string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern): this
```

Set current fill style. Provide a valid color string such as `"#FFF"` or `"rgba(255,0,100,0.5)"` or `false` to specify no fill color.

**Parameters**

- `c` (`string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern`) — fill color which can be as color, gradient, or pattern. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/fillStyle))

**Example**

```ts
form.fill("#F90")`, `form.fill("rgba(0,0,0,.5")`, `form.fill(false)
```

##### `fillOnly`

*overrides `VisualForm.fillOnly`*

```ts
fillOnly(c: string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern): this
```

Set current fill style and remove stroke style.

**Parameters**

- `c` (`string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern`) — fill color which can be as color, gradient, or pattern. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/fillStyle))

<a id="canvas-canvasform-font"></a>
##### `font`

*overrides `VisualForm.font`*

```ts
font(sizeOrFont: number | Font, weight: string, style: string, lineHeight: number, family: string): this
```

Set the current font.

**Parameters**

- `sizeOrFont` (`number | Font`) — either a number to specify font-size, or a `Font` object to specify all font properties
- `weight` (`string`) — Optional font-weight string such as "bold"
- `style` (`string`) — Optional font-style string such as "italic"
- `lineHeight` (`number`) — Optional line-height number suchas 1.5
- `family` (`string`) — Optional font-family such as "Helvetica, sans-serif"

**Example**

```ts
form.font( myFont )`, `form.font(14, "bold")
```

<a id="canvas-canvasform-font-width-estimate"></a>
##### `fontWidthEstimate`

```ts
fontWidthEstimate(estimate: boolean | sample | char = true): this
```

Set whether to use html canvas' [`measureText`](#svg-svgcontext2d-measure-text) function, or a faster but less accurate estimate.

**Parameters**

- `estimate` (`boolean | sample | char`; default `true`) — `false` to use ctx.measureText; `true` or `"sample"` to use a sampled-average estimator (fastest); `"char"` to use a per-character width cache (nearly as accurate as measureText for most texts, and much faster after warmup)

<a id="canvas-canvasform-get-text-width"></a>
##### `getTextWidth`

```ts
getTextWidth(c: string): number
```

Get the width of this text. It will return an actual measurement or an estimate based on [`fontWidthEstimate`](#canvas-canvasform-font-width-estimate) setting. Default is an actual measurement using canvas context's measureText.

**Parameters**

- `c` (`string`) — a string of text contents

<a id="canvas-canvasform-gradient"></a>
##### `gradient`

```ts
gradient(stops: string[] | number,string[]):  Fn(area1:GroupLike, area2:GroupLike)
```

This function takes an array of gradient colors, and returns a function to define the areas of the gradient fill. See demo code in [CanvasForm.gradient](https://ptsjs.org/demo/?name=canvasform.textBox).

**Parameters**

- `stops` (`string[] | number,string[]`) — an array of gradient stops. This can be an array of colors `["#f00", "#0f0", ...]` for evenly distributed gradient, or an array of [stop, color] like `[[0.1, "#f00"], [0.7, "#0f0"]]`

**Returns:** a function that takes 1 or 2 `Group` as parameters. Use a single `Group` to specify a rectangular area for linear gradient, or use 2 `Groups` to specify 2 `Circles` for radial gradient.

**Example**

```ts
c1 = Circle.fromCenter(...); grad = form.gradient(["#f00", "#00f"]); form.fill( grad( c1, c2 ) ).circle( c1 )
```

<a id="canvas-canvasform-image"></a>
##### `image`

```ts
image(ptOrRect: PtLikeIterable | PtLike, img: Img | CanvasImageSource, orig: PtLikeIterable): CanvasForm
```

Draw an image.

**Parameters**

- `ptOrRect` (`PtLikeIterable | PtLike`) — a target area to place the image. Either a PtLike specifying a position, or a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt (top-left position, bottom-right position) that specifies a bounding box. Default is (0,0) at top-left.
- `img` (`Img | CanvasImageSource`) — either an [Img](#image-img) instance or an [`CanvasImageSource`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasImageSource) instance (eg the image from `<img>`, `<video>` or `<canvas>`)
- `orig` (`PtLikeIterable`) — optionally a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt (top-left position, bottom-right position) that specifies a cropping box  in the original target.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-image-data"></a>
##### `imageData`

```ts
imageData(ptOrRect: PtLikeIterable | PtLike, img: ImageData): CanvasForm
```

Draw ImageData on canvas using ImageData

**Parameters**

- `ptOrRect` (`PtLikeIterable | PtLike`) — a target area to place the image. Either a Pt or numeric array specifying a position, or a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt (top-left, bottom-right) that specifies a bounding box for resizing. Default is (0,0) at top-left.
- `img` (`ImageData`) — an ImageData object

<a id="canvas-canvasform-log"></a>
##### `log`

```ts
log(txt: any): this
```

A convenient way to draw some text on canvas for logging or debugging. It'll be draw on the top-left of the canvas as an overlay.

**Parameters**

<a id="canvas-canvasform-paragraph-box"></a>
##### `paragraphBox`

```ts
paragraphBox(box: PtLikeIterable, txt: string, lineHeight: number = 1.2, verticalAlign: TextVerticalAlign = "top", crop: boolean = true): this
```

Fit multi-line text in a rectangular box. Note that this will also set canvas context's textBaseline to "top".

**Parameters**

- `box` (`PtLikeIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt that represents a bounding box
- `txt` (`string`) — string of text
- `lineHeight` (`number`; default `1.2`) — line height as a ratio of font size. Default is 1.2.
- `verticalAlign` (`TextVerticalAlign`; default `"top"`) — "top", "middle", or "bottom" to specify vertical alignment inside the box
- `crop` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean to specify whether to crop text when overflowing

<a id="canvas-canvasform-stroke"></a>
##### `stroke`

*overrides `VisualForm.stroke`*

```ts
stroke(c: string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern, width: number, linejoin: CanvasLineJoin, linecap: CanvasLineCap): this
```

Set current stroke style. Provide a valid color string or `false` to specify no stroke color.

**Parameters**

- `c` (`string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern`) — stroke color which can be as color, gradient, or pattern. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/strokeStyle))
- `width` (`number`) — Optional value (can be floating point) to set line width
- `linejoin` (`CanvasLineJoin`) — Optional string to set line joint style. Can be "miter", "bevel", or "round".
- `linecap` (`CanvasLineCap`) — Optional string to set line cap style. Can be "butt", "round", or "square".

**Example**

```ts
form.stroke("#F90")`, `form.stroke("rgba(0,0,0,.5")`, `form.stroke(false)`, `form.stroke("#000", 0.5, 'round', 'square')
```


Set stroke style and remove fill style.

**Parameters**

- `c` (`string | boolean | CanvasGradient | CanvasPattern`) — stroke color which can be as color, gradient, or pattern. (See [canvas documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasRenderingContext2D/strokeStyle))
- `width` (`number`) — Optional value (can be floating point) to set line width
- `linejoin` (`CanvasLineJoin`) — Optional string to set line joint style. Can be "miter", "bevel", or "round".
- `linecap` (`CanvasLineCap`) — Optional string to set line cap style. Can be "butt", "round", or "square".

##### `text`

<a id="canvas-canvasform-text-box"></a>
##### `textBox`

```ts
textBox(box: PtIterable, txt: string, verticalAlign: TextVerticalAlign = "middle", tail: string = "", overrideBaseline: boolean = true): this
```

Fit a single-line text in a rectangular box.

**Parameters**

- `box` (`PtIterable`) — a rectangle box defined by a Group or an Iterable<Pt>
- `txt` (`string`) — string of text
- `verticalAlign` (`TextVerticalAlign`; default `"middle"`) — "top", "middle", or "bottom" to specify vertical alignment inside the box
- `tail` (`string`; default `""`) — text to indicate overflow such as "...". Default is empty "".
- `overrideBaseline` (`boolean`; default `true`) — If `true`, use the corresponding baseline as verticalAlign. If `false`, use the current canvas context's textBaseline setting. Default is `true`.

<a id="canvas-canvasform-use-offscreen"></a>
##### `useOffscreen`

```ts
useOffscreen(off: boolean = true, clear: string | boolean = false): CanvasForm
```

Toggle whether to draw on offscreen canvas (if offscreen is set in CanvasSpace)

**Parameters**

- `off` (`boolean`; default `true`) — if `true`, draw on offscreen canvas instead of the visible canvas. Default is `true`
- `clear` (`string | boolean`; default `false`) — optionally provide a valid color string to fill a bg color. see CanvasSpace's `clearOffscreen` function.

- `ctx` (`RenderingContext2D`) — canvas rendering context
- `ptOrRect` (`PtLikeIterable | PtLike`) — a target area to place the image. Either a Pt or numeric array specifying a position, or a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt (top-left, bottom-right) that specifies a bounding box for resizing. Default is (0,0) at top-left.
- `img` (`Img | CanvasImageSource`) — either an [Img](#image-img) instance or an [`CanvasImageSource`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/CanvasImageSource) instance (eg the image from `<img>`, `<video>` or `<canvas>`)
- `orig` (`PtLikeIterable`) — optionally a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt (top-left, bottom-right) that specifies a cropping box in the original target.

<a id="canvas-canvasspace"></a>
### `CanvasSpace`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Canvas.ts:26`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Canvas.ts#L26)

**Extends:** `MultiTouchSpace`

CanvasSpace is an implementation of the abstract class [`Space`](#space-space). It represents a space for HTML Canvas.
Learn more about the concept of Space in [this guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Space-0500.html).

#### Constructors

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new CanvasSpace(elem: string | Element, callback: Function): CanvasSpace
```

Create a CanvasSpace which represents a HTML Canvas Space

**Parameters**

- `elem` (`string | Element`) — Specify an element by its "id" attribute as string, or by the element object itself. An element can be an existing `<canvas>`, or a `<div>` container in which a new `<canvas>` will be created. If left empty, a `<div id="pt_container"><canvas id="pt" /></div>` will be added to DOM. Use css to customize its appearance if needed.
- `callback` (`Function`) — an optional callback `function(boundingBox, spaceElement)` to be called when canvas is appended and ready. Alternatively, a "ready" event will also be fired from the `<canvas>` element when it's appended, which can be traced with `spaceInstance.canvas.addEventListener("ready")`

**Example**

```ts
new CanvasSpace( "#myElementID" )
```

#### Accessors


Set whether the canvas element should resize when its container is resized.

Get the html canvas element

Get the offscreen canvas element


**See also:** `CanvasForm`

##### `playItems`

*protected · overrides `MultiTouchSpace.playItems`*

```ts
playItems(time: number): void
```

Main animation function.

**Parameters**

- `time` (`number`) — current time

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-recorder"></a>
##### `recorder`

```ts
recorder(downloadOrCallback: boolean |  Fn(blobURL:string), filetype: string = "webm", bitrate: number = 15000000): MediaRecorder
```

Get a [`MediaRecorder`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaRecorder) to record the current CanvasSpace. You can then call its `start()` function to start recording, and `stop()` to either download the video file or handle the blob data in the callback function you provided.

**Parameters**

- `downloadOrCallback` (`boolean |  Fn(blobURL:string)`) — Either `true` to download the video, or provide a callback function to handle the Blob data, when recording is completed.
- `filetype` (`string`; default `"webm"`) — video format. Default is "webm".
- `bitrate` (`number`; default `15000000`) — bitrate per second

**Example**

```ts
let rec = space.recorder(true); rec.start(); setTimeout( () => rec.stop(), 5000); // record 5s of video and download the file
```

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-resize"></a>
##### `resize`

*overrides `MultiTouchSpace.resize`*

```ts
resize(b: Bound, evt: Event): this
```

This overrides Space's `resize` function. It's used as a callback function for window's resize event and not usually called directly. You can keep track of resize events with `resize: (bound ,evt)` callback in your player objects.

**Parameters**

- `b` (`Bound`) — a Bound object to resize to
- `evt` (`Event`) — Optionally pass a resize event

**See also:** Space.add

<a id="canvas-canvasspace-setup"></a>
##### `setup`

```ts
setup(opt: CanvasSpaceOptions): this
```

Set up various options for CanvasSpace. The `opt` parameter is an object with the following fields. This is usually set during instantiation, eg `new CanvasSpace(...).setup( { opt } )`

**Parameters**

- `opt` (`CanvasSpaceOptions`) — a [`CanvasSpaceOptions`](#types-canvasspaceoptions) object with optional settings, ie `{ bgcolor:string, resize:boolean, retina:boolean, offscreen:boolean, pixelDensity:number }`.

**Example**

```ts
space.setup({ bgcolor: "#f00", retina: true, resize: true })
```

## Module: `Color`

<a id="color-color"></a>
### `Color`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Color.ts:11`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Color.ts#L11)

**Extends:** `Pt`

Color is a subclass of Pt. Since a color in a color space is analogous to a point or vector in a space, you can apply all Pt operations to colors too. The Color class provides support for many color spaces like HSL and LAB.

**Parameters**

- `args` (`any[]`) — Pt-like parameters which can be a list of numeric parameters, an array of numbers, or an object with {x,y,z,w} properties

<a id="create-delaunay"></a>
### `Delaunay`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Create.ts:912`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Create.ts#L912)

**Extends:** `Group`

Delaunay is a [`Group`](#pt-group) of Pts that generates Delaunay and Voronoi tessellations.
The triangulation core is adapted from [Delaunator](https://github.com/mapbox/delaunator)
(ISC License, © Mapbox); earlier versions were based on
[Paul Bourke's algorithm](http://paulbourke.net/papers/triangulate/).

#### Methods

<a id="create-delaunay-delaunay"></a>
##### `delaunay`

```ts
delaunay(triangleOnly: boolean = true): GroupLike[] | DelaunayShape[]
```

Generate Delaunay triangles. This function also caches the mesh that is used to generate Voronoi tessellation in `voronoi()`. See a [Delaunay demo here](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=create.delaunay).

**Parameters**

- `triangleOnly` (`boolean`; default `true`) — if true, returns an array of triangles in Groups, otherwise return the whole DelaunayShape

**Returns:** an array of Groups or an array of DelaunayShapes `{i, j, k, triangle, circle}` which records the indices of the vertices, and the calculated triangles and circumcircles

<a id="create-delaunay-mesh"></a>
##### `mesh`

```ts
mesh(): DelaunayMesh
```

Get the cached mesh. The mesh is an array of objects, each of which representing the enclosing triangles around a Pt in this Delaunay group.

**Returns:** an array of objects that store a series of DelaunayShapes

<a id="create-delaunay-neighbor-pts"></a>
##### `neighborPts`

```ts
neighborPts(i: number, sort: boolean = false): GroupLike
```

Given an index of a Pt in this Delaunay Group, returns its neighboring Pts in the network.

**Parameters**

- `i` (`number`) — index of a Pt
- `sort` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if true, sort the neighbors so that their edges will form a polygon

**Returns:** an array of Pts

<a id="create-delaunay-neighbors"></a>
##### `neighbors`

```ts
neighbors(i: number): DelaunayShape[]
```

Given an index of a Pt in this Delaunay Group, returns its neighboring DelaunayShapes.

**Parameters**

- `i` (`number`) — index of a Pt

**Returns:** an array of DelaunayShapes `{i, j, k, triangle, circle}`

<a id="create-delaunay-voronoi"></a>
##### `voronoi`

```ts
voronoi(bound: PtIterable): Group[]
```

Generate Voronoi cells. `delaunay()` must be called before calling this function. See a [Voronoi demo here](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=create.delaunay).

**Parameters**

- `bound` (`PtIterable`) — Optionally provide a rectangular bound (eg, `space.innerBound`) to clip the cells against. Without a bound, cells around sliver triangles can extend to enormous coordinates (circumcenters of nearly-collinear points), which is technically correct but extremely slow to draw.

**Returns:** an array of Groups, each of which represents a Voronoi cell

## Module: `Dom`

<a id="dom-domspace"></a>
### `DOMSpace`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Dom.ts:33`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Dom.ts#L33)

**Extends:** `MultiTouchSpace`

DOMSpace hosts a Space in a DOM element. It is the subclassing entry point for building
custom element-based spaces; usually its subclass [`SVGSpace`](#svg-svgspace) should be used instead.
Learn more about spaces in [this guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/space-0500).

When using a Space inside a component framework, create it on mount and call
[`DOMSpace.dispose`](#dom-domspace-dispose) on unmount so listeners and the animation loop are released.
For example, in React:
```
useEffect(() => {
  const space = new SVGSpace(ref.current).setup({ resize: true });
  space.add(...).play();
  return () => { space.dispose(); };
}, []);
```
Dispose is idempotent, and a new Space can be mounted on the same element afterwards
(as happens under React's StrictMode).

#### Constructors

<a id="dom-domspace-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new DOMSpace(elem: string | Element, callback: Function): DOMSpace
```

Create a DOMSpace for HTML DOM elements

**Parameters**

- `elem` (`string | Element`) — Specify an element by its "id" attribute as string, or by the element object itself. Use css to customize its appearance if needed.
- `callback` (`Function`) — an optional callback `function(boundingBox, spaceElement)` to be called when element is appended and ready. Alternatively, a "ready" event will also be fired from the element when it's appended, which can be traced with `spaceInstance.element.addEventListener("ready")`

**Example**

```ts
new DOMSpace( "#myElementID" )
```

##### `clear`

*overrides `MultiTouchSpace.clear`*


##### `dispose`

```ts

```

Dispose of browser resources held by this space and remove all players. Call this before
unmounting the DOM, eg in a framework component's unmount/cleanup callback. Dispose is
idempotent, and a new Space can be created on the same element afterwards.

This overrides Space's `resize` function. It's used as a callback function for window's resize event and not usually called directly. You can keep track of resize events with `resize: (bound, evt)` callback in your player objects (See [`Space.add`](#space-space-add) function).

- `evt` (`Event`) — Optionally pass a resize event

<a id="dom-domspace-setup"></a>
##### `setup`

```ts
setup(opt: { bgcolor:string, resize:boolean }): this
```

Set up various options for DOMSpace. This is usually set during instantiation, eg `new DOMSpace(...).setup( {opt} )`.

**Parameters**

- `opt` (`{ bgcolor:string, resize:boolean }`) — an object with these optional properties: **bgcolor** is a hex or rgba string to set initial background color of the canvas, or use `false` or "transparent" to set a transparent background; **resize** a boolean to set whether `<canvas>` size should auto resize to match its container's size, which can also be set using `autoSize()`.

**Example**

```ts
space.setup({ bgcolor: "#f00", resize: true })
```

A static function to add a DOM element inside a node. Usually you don't need to use this directly. See methods in [`HTMLForm`](#dom-htmlform) instead.

**Parameters**

- `parent` (`Element`) — the parent element, or `null` to use current `<svg>` as parent.
- `name` (`string`) — a string of element name,  such as `rect` or `circle`
- `id` (`string`) — id attribute of the new element
- `autoClass` (`boolean`; default `true`) — add a class based on the id (from char 0 to index of "-"). Default is true.

<a id="form-font"></a>
### `Font`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Form.ts:262`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Form.ts#L262)

Font class lets you create a specific font style with properties for its size and style. A font instance can be passed as parameter to set a form's font. For example, see [`CanvasForm.font`](#canvas-canvasform-font).

#### Constructors

<a id="form-font-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new Font(size: number = 12, face: string = "sans-serif", weight: string = "", style: string = "", lineHeight: number = 1.5): Font
```

Create a font style.

**Parameters**

- `size` (`number`; default `12`) — font size. Defaults is 12px.
- `face` (`string`; default `"sans-serif"`) — Optional font-family, use css-like string such as "Helvetica" or "Helvetica, sans-serif". Default is "sans-serif".
- `weight` (`string`; default `""`) — Optional font weight such as "bold". Default is "" (none).
- `style` (`string`; default `""`) — Optional font style such as "italic". Default is "" (none).
- `lineHeight` (`number`; default `1.5`) — Optional line height. Default is 1.5.

**Example**

```ts
new Font(12, "Frutiger, sans-serif", "bold", "underline", 1.5)
```

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Form.ts:25`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Form.ts#L25)

<a id="module-image"></a>
## Module: `Image`

<a id="image-img"></a>
### `Img`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Image.ts:25`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Image.ts#L25)

Img provides convenient functions to support image operations on HTML Canvas and [`CanvasSpace`](#canvas-canvasspace). Combine this with other Pts functions to experiment with visual forms that integrate bitmaps and vector graphics.

#### Constructors

<a id="image-img-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new Img(editable: boolean | ImgOptions = false, space: CanvasSpace, crossOrigin: boolean): Img
```

Create an Img

**Parameters**

- `editable` (`boolean | ImgOptions`; default `false`) — either an [`ImgOptions`](#image-imgoptions) object, or a boolean specifying if you want to manipulate pixels of this image. Default is `false`.
- `space` (`CanvasSpace`) — Set the `CanvasSpace` reference. This is optional but will make sure the image's pixelScale match the canvas and set the context for creating pattern.
- `crossOrigin` (`boolean`) — an optional parameter to enable loading cross-domain images if set to true. The image server's configuration must also be set correctly. For more, see [this documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/CORS_enabled_image).

**Example**

```ts
new Img(true, space)`, `new Img({ editable: true, pixelScale: 2 })
```

#### Accessors

##### `canvas`

```ts
get canvas(): HTMLCanvasElement
```

Get the internal canvas


Get size of the canvas

Get the original image

<a id="image-img-static-load"></a>
##### `load`

*static*

```ts
static load(src: string, editable: boolean | ImgOptions = false, space: CanvasSpace, ready:  Fn(img:Img)): Promise
```

A static function to load an image, returning a Promise that resolves to the loaded Img.
A load failure rejects the Promise.

**Parameters**

- `src` (`string`) — an url of the image in same domain. Alternatively you can use a base64 string. To load from Blob, use `Img.fromBlob`.
- `editable` (`boolean | ImgOptions`; default `false`) — either an [`ImgOptions`](#image-imgoptions) object, or a boolean specifying if you want to manipulate pixels of this image. Default is `false`.
- `space` (`CanvasSpace`) — Set the `CanvasSpace` reference. This is optional but will make sure the image's pixelScale match the canvas and set the context for creating pattern.
- `ready` (` Fn(img:Img)`) — An optional callback, invoked with the Img when loading succeeds

**Example**

```ts
const img = await Img.load("photo.jpg", true)
```

<a id="image-img-static-load-async"></a>
##### `loadAsync`

*static*

```ts
static loadAsync(src: string, editable: boolean | ImgOptions = false, space: CanvasSpace): Promise
```

A static method to load an image using async/await.

**Parameters**

- `src` (`string`) — an url of the image in same domain. Alternatively you can use a base64 string. To load from Blob, use `Img.fromBlob`.
- `editable` (`boolean | ImgOptions`; default `false`) — Specify if you want to manipulate pixels of this image. Default is `false`.
- `space` (`CanvasSpace`) — Set the `CanvasSpace` reference. This is optional but will make sure the image's pixelScale match the canvas and set the context for creating pattern.

**deprecated:** Use [`Img.load`](#image-img-load), which now returns a Promise.

<a id="image-img-static-load-pattern"></a>
##### `loadPattern`

*static*

```ts
static loadPattern(src: string, space: CanvasSpace, repeat: CanvasPatternRepetition = "repeat", editable: boolean = false): Promise
```

A static method to load an image pattern using async/await.

**Parameters**

- `src` (`string`) — an url of the image in same domain. Alternatively you can use a base64 string. To load from Blob, use `Img.fromBlob`.
- `space` (`CanvasSpace`) — Set the `CanvasSpace` reference. This is optional but will make sure the image's pixelScale match the canvas and set the context for creating pattern.
- `repeat` (`CanvasPatternRepetition`; default `"repeat"`) — set how the pattern will repeat fills
- `editable` (`boolean`; default `false`) — Specify if you want to manipulate pixels of this image. Default is `false`.

**Returns:** a `CanvasPattern` instance for use in `fill()`

**Kind:** Typealias · **Source:** [`src/Image.ts:11`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Image.ts#L11)

Options for creating an [`Img`](#image-img).

```ts
type ImgOptions = { crossOrigin:boolean, editable:boolean, pixelScale:number, space:CanvasSpace };
```

### `Mat`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/LinearAlgebra.ts:210`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/LinearAlgebra.ts#L210)

Mat provides various static functions for matrix operations as well as a convenient way to chain a 3x3 transformation matrix. It's not fully optimized but good enough to use.

#### Constructors

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new Mat(): Mat
```

#### Accessors

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-dom-matrix"></a>

```ts

```

Convert the value of its stored 3x3 matrix to a 2D [`DOMMatrix`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DOMMatrix) instance

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-value"></a>
##### `value`

```ts
get value(): GroupLike
```

Get the current value of its stored 3x3 matrix

#### Methods

```ts

```

Reset the internal 3x3 matrix to its identity

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-rotate2-d"></a>

```ts
rotate2D(ang: number, at: PtLike = ...): this
```

Scale the internal 3x3 matrix. You can chain this function with other related functions.

**Parameters**

- `at` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — Optional origin location to rotate from.

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-scale2-d"></a>
##### `scale2D`

```ts
scale2D(val: PtLike, at: PtLike = ...): this
```

Scale the internal 3x3 matrix. You can chain this function with other related functions.

**Parameters**

- `val` (`PtLike`) — [x, y] scale factors
- `at` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — Optional origin location to scale from.

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-shear2-d"></a>
##### `shear2D`

```ts
shear2D(val: PtLike, at: PtLike = ...): this
```

Shear the internal 3x3 matrix. You can chain this function with other related functions.

**Parameters**

- `val` (`PtLike`) — [x, y] shear factors (before tan() operation)
- `at` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — Optional origin location to scale from.

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-translate2-d"></a>
##### `translate2D`

```ts
translate2D(val: PtLike): this
```

Translate the internal 3x3 matrix. You can chain this function with other related functions.

**Parameters**

- `val` (`PtLike`) — [x, y] offset values

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-static-add"></a>
##### `add`

*static*

```ts
static add(a: GroupLike, b: number | GroupLike | number[][]): Group
```

Matrix addition. Matrices should have the same rows and columns.

**Parameters**

- `a` (`GroupLike`) — a group of Pt
- `b` (`number | GroupLike | number[][]`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a group of Pt

**Returns:** a new group with the same rows and columns as a and b

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-static-multiply"></a>
##### `multiply`

*static*

```ts
static multiply(a: GroupLike, b: number | GroupLike | number[][], transposed: boolean = false, elementwise: boolean = false): Group
```

Matrix multiplication.

**Parameters**

- `a` (`GroupLike`) — a Group of M Pts, each with K dimensions (M-rows, K-columns)
- `b` (`number | GroupLike | number[][]`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a Group of K Pts, each with N dimensions (K-rows, N-columns) -- or if transposed is true, then N Pts with K dimensions
- `transposed` (`boolean`; default `false`) — (Only applicable if it's not elementwise multiplication) If true, then a and b's columns should match (ie, each Pt should have the same dimensions). Default is `false`.
- `elementwise` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if true, then the multiplication is done element-wise. Default is `false`.

**Returns:** If not elementwise, this will return a new group with M Pt, each with N dimensions (M-rows, N-columns).


Same as `zip` function.

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-static-zip"></a>
##### `zip`

*static*

```ts
static zip(g: GroupLike | number[][], defaultValue: number | boolean = false, useLongest: boolean = false): Group
```

Zip a group of Pt. For example, `[[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]]` will become `[[1,3,5],[2,4,6]]`.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`GroupLike | number[][]`) — a group of Pt
- `defaultValue` (`number | boolean`; default `false`) — a default value to fill if index out of bound. If not provided, it will throw an error instead.
- `useLongest` (`boolean`; default `false`) — If true, find the longest list of values in a Pt and use its length for zipping. Default is false, which uses the first item's length for zipping.

<a id="linearalgebra-mat-static-zip-slice"></a>
##### `zipSlice`

*static*

```ts
static zipSlice(g: GroupLike | number[][], index: number, defaultValue: number | boolean = false): Pt
```

Zip one slice of an array of Pts. For example, if the input `g` are organized in rows, then this function will take the values in a specific column.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`GroupLike | number[][]`) — a group of Pt
- `index` (`number`)
- `defaultValue` (`number | boolean`; default `false`) — a default value to fill if index out of bound. If not provided, it will throw an error instead.

<a id="num-range"></a>
### `Range`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Num.ts:949`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Num.ts#L949)

Range object keeps track of a Group of n-dimensional Pts to provide its minimum, maximum, and magnitude in each dimension.
It also provides convenient functions such as mapping the Group to another range. This class may be useful for visualizing data in charts.

#### Constructors

<a id="num-range-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new Range(g: PtIterable): Range
```

Construct a Range instance for a Group of Pts.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt>

#### Accessors

<a id="num-range-magnitude"></a>
##### `magnitude`

```ts
get magnitude(): Pt
```

Get this Range's magnitude in each dimension.

<a id="num-range-max"></a>
##### `max`

```ts
get max(): Pt
```

Get this Range's maximum values per dimension.

<a id="num-range-min"></a>
##### `min`

```ts
get min(): Pt
```

Get this Range's minimum values per dimension.

#### Methods

<a id="num-range-append"></a>
##### `append`

```ts
append(pts: PtLikeIterable, update: boolean = true): this
```

Add more Pts to this Range and recalculate its min and max values.

**Parameters**

- `pts` (`PtLikeIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> to append to this Range
- `update` (`boolean`; default `true`) — Optional. Set the parameter to `false` if you want to append without immediately updating this Range's min and max values. Default is `true`.

<a id="num-range-calc"></a>
##### `calc`

```ts
calc(): this
```

Go through the group and find its min and max values. Usually you don't need to call this function directly.

<a id="num-range-map-to"></a>
##### `mapTo`

```ts
mapTo(min: number, max: number, exclude: boolean[]): Group
```

Map this Range to another range of values.

**Parameters**

- `min` (`number`) — target range's minimum value
- `max` (`number`) — target range's maximum value
- `exclude` (`boolean[]`) — Optional boolean array where `true` means excluding the conversion in that specific dimension.

<a id="num-range-ticks"></a>
##### `ticks`

```ts
ticks(count: number): Group
```

Create a number of evenly spaced "ticks" that span this Range's min and max value.

**Parameters**

- `count` (`number`) — number of subdivision. For example, 10 subdivision will return 11 tick values, which include first(min) and last(max) values.

##### `cubicBezier`

*static*

```ts
static cubicBezier(t: number, c: number = 1, p1: PtLike = ..., p2: PtLike = ...): number
```

Cubic bezier curve. This reuses the bezier functions in Curve class. Note that `t` is the curve parameter, not the x position: unlike CSS `cubic-bezier(...)`, this returns the curve's y value at parameter `t` rather than solving y at x = t.

**Parameters**

- `t` (`number`) — a value between 0 to 1
- `c` (`number`; default `1`) — the value to shape, default is 1
- `p1` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — ` a Pt object specifying the first control Pt. Default is `Pt(0.1, 0.7).
- `p2` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — ` a Pt object specifying the second control Pt. Default is `Pt(0.9, 0.2).

<a id="module-op"></a>
## Module: `Op`

<a id="op-circle"></a>
### `Circle`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:678`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L678)

Circle class provides static functions to create and operate on circles. A circle is usually represented as a Group of 2 Pts, where the first Pt specifies the center, and the second Pt specifies the radius.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.

#### Methods

<a id="op-circle-static-from-center"></a>
##### `fromCenter`

*static*

```ts
static fromCenter(pt: PtLike, radius: number): Group
```

Create a circle based on a center point and a radius.

**Parameters**

- `pt` (`PtLike`) — center point of circle
- `radius` (`number`) — radius of circle

**Returns:** a Group that represents a circle

<a id="op-circle-static-from-rect"></a>
##### `fromRect`

*static*

```ts
static fromRect(pts: PtLikeIterable, enclose: boolean = false): Group
```

Create a circle that either fits within, or encloses, a rectangle.

**Parameters**

- `pts` (`PtLikeIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<PtLike> with 2 Pt representing a rectangle
- `enclose` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if `true`, the circle will enclose the rectangle. Default is `false`, which will fit the circle inside the rectangle.

**Returns:** a Group that represents a circle

<a id="op-circle-static-from-triangle"></a>
##### `fromTriangle`

*static*

```ts
static fromTriangle(pts: PtIterable, enclose: boolean = false): Group
```

Create a circle that either fits within, or encloses, a triangle. Same as [`Triangle.circumcircle`](#op-triangle-static-circumcircle) or [`Triangle.incircle`](#op-triangle-static-incircle).

**Parameters**

- `pts` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> with 3 Pt representing a rectangle
- `enclose` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if `true`, the circle will enclose the triangle. Default is `false`, which will fit the circle inside the triangle.

**Returns:** a Group that represents a circle

For more optimized implementation, store the rectangle's sides separately (eg, [`Rectangle.sides`](#op-rectangle-static-sides)) and use [`Polygon.intersectPolygon2D()`](#op-polygon-static-intersect-polygon2-d).

**Parameters**

- `circle` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> with 2 Pt representing a circle
- `rect` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> with 2 Pt representing a rectangle

**Returns:** a Group of intersection points, or an empty Group if no intersection is found

<a id="op-curve"></a>
### `Curve`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:1691`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L1691)

Curve class provides static functions to interpolate curves. A curve is usually represented as a Group of 3 or more control points.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.

#### Methods

<a id="op-curve-static-bezier"></a>
##### `bezier`

*static*

```ts
static bezier(pts: GroupLike, steps: number = 10): Group
```

Create a Bezier curve. In a cubic bezier curve, the first and 4th anchors are end-points, and 2nd and 3rd anchors are control-points.

**Parameters**

- `pts` (`GroupLike`) — a group of anchor Pt
- `steps` (`number`; default `10`) — the number of line segments per curve. Defaults to 10 steps.

**Returns:** a curve as a group of interpolated Pt

<a id="op-curve-static-bezier-step"></a>
##### `bezierStep`

*static*

```ts
static bezierStep(step: Pt, ctrls: GroupLike): Pt
```

Interpolate to get a point on a cubic Bezier curve.

**Parameters**

- `step` (`Pt`) — the coefficients [t*t*t, t*t, t, 1]
- `ctrls` (`GroupLike`) — a group of anchor Pts

**Returns:** an interpolated Pt on the curve

<a id="op-curve-static-bspline"></a>
##### `bspline`

*static*

```ts
static bspline(pts: GroupLike, steps: number = 10, tension: number = 1): Group
```

Create a basis spline (NURBS) curve.

**Parameters**

- `pts` (`GroupLike`) — a group of anchor Pt
- `steps` (`number`; default `10`) — the number of line segments per curve. Defaults to 10 steps.
- `tension` (`number`; default `1`) — optional value between 0 to n to specify a "tension". Default is 1 which is the usual tension.

**Returns:** a curve as a group of interpolated Pt

<a id="op-curve-static-bspline-step"></a>
##### `bsplineStep`

*static*

```ts
static bsplineStep(step: Pt, ctrls: GroupLike): Pt
```

Interpolate to get a point on a basis spline curve.

**Parameters**

- `step` (`Pt`) — the coefficients [t*t*t, t*t, t, 1]
- `ctrls` (`GroupLike`) — a group of anchor Pts

**Returns:** an interpolated Pt on the curve

<a id="op-curve-static-bspline-tension-step"></a>
##### `bsplineTensionStep`

*static*

```ts
static bsplineTensionStep(step: Pt, ctrls: GroupLike, tension: number = 1): Pt
```

Interpolate to get a point on a basis spline curve with tension.

**Parameters**

- `step` (`Pt`) — the coefficients [t*t*t, t*t, t, 1]
- `ctrls` (`GroupLike`) — a group of anchor Pts
- `tension` (`number`; default `1`) — optional value between 0 to n to specify a "tension". Default to 1 which is the usual tension.

**Returns:** an interpolated Pt on the curve

<a id="op-curve-static-cardinal"></a>

*static*

Create a Cardinal curve.

- `pts` (`PtLikeIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<PtLike>
- `steps` (`number`; default `10`) — the number of line segments per curve. Defaults to 10 steps.
- `tension` (`number`; default `0.5`) — optional value between 0 to 1 to specify a "tension". Default to 0.5 which is the tension for Catmull-Rom curve.

**Returns:** a curve as a group of interpolated Pt

<a id="op-curve-static-cardinal-step"></a>
##### `cardinalStep`

- `steps` (`number`; default `10`) — the number of line segments per curve. Defaults to 10 steps

<a id="op-line"></a>
### `Line`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:25`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L25)

Line class provides static functions to create and operate on lines. A line is usually represented as a Group of 2 Pts.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.

#### Methods

<a id="op-line-static-collinear"></a>
##### `collinear`

*static*

```ts
static collinear(p1: PtLike, p2: PtLike, p3: PtLike, threshold: number = 0.01): boolean
```

Check if three Pts are collinear, ie, on the same straight path.

**Parameters**

- `p1` (`PtLike`) — first Pt
- `p2` (`PtLike`) — second Pt
- `p3` (`PtLike`) — third Pt
- `threshold` (`number`; default `0.01`) — a threshold where a smaller value means higher precision threshold for the straight line. Default is 0.01.

<a id="op-line-static-crop"></a>
##### `crop`

*static*

```ts
static crop(line: PtIterable, size: PtLike, index: number = 0, cropAsCircle: boolean = true): Pt
```

Crop this line by a circle or rectangle at end points. This can be useful for creating arrows that connect to an object's edge.

**Parameters**

- `line` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> representing a line to crop
- `size` (`PtLike`) — size of circle or rectangle as Pt
- `index` (`number`; default `0`) — line's end point index, ie, 0 = start and 1 = end.
- `cropAsCircle` (`boolean`; default `true`) — a boolean to specify whether the `size` parameter should be treated as circle. Default is `true`.

**Returns:** an intersecting point on the line that can be used for cropping.

<a id="op-line-static-distance-from-pt"></a>
##### `distanceFromPt`

*static*

```ts
static distanceFromPt(line: GroupLike, pt: PtLike): number
```

Given a line and a point, find the shortest distance from the point to the line.

**Parameters**

- `line` (`GroupLike`) — a Group of 2 Pts
- `pt` (`PtLike`) — a Pt

**See also:** `Line.perpendicularFromPt`

*static*

Create a line that originates from an anchor point, given an angle and a magnitude.

- `magnitude` (`number`) — magnitude of the line

- `p2` (`PtLike`) — line's second end point

*static*

*static*



*static*


Find intersection points of 2 sets of lines. This checks all line segments in the two lists. Consider using a bounding-box check before calling this. - `lines2` (`Iterable`) — an Array/Iterable of (Groups or Iterables<Pt>)

<a id="op-polygon"></a>
### `Polygon`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:1053`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L1053)

Polygon class provides static functions to create and operate on polygons. A polygon is usually represented as a Group of 3 or more Pts.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.
See [Op guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Op-0400.html) for details.

- `poly` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt>
- `index` (`number`) — the target Pt
- `closePath` (`boolean`; default `false`) — a boolean to specify whether the polygon should be closed (ie, whether the final segment should be counted).


- `index` (`number`) — the Pt in the polygon to bisect from


*static*

### `Rectangle`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Op.ts:420`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Op.ts#L420)

Rectangle class provides static functions to create and operate on rectangles. A rectangle is usually represented as a Group of 2 Pts, marking the top-left and bottom-right corners of the rectangle.
You can use the static functions as-is, or apply the [`Group.op`](#pt-group-op) or [`Pt.op`](#pt-pt-op) to enable functional programming.

<a id="physics-body"></a>
### `Body`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Physics.ts:885`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Physics.ts#L885)

**Extends:** `Group`

Body is a subclass of [`Group`](#pt-group) that stores a set of [`Particle`](#physics-particle)s and edge constraints. It is usually added into a [`World`](#physics-world) to create physics simulations.
See [a demo here](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=physics.shapes).

#### Constructors







**Parameters**

<a id="physics-body-solve-edges"></a>
##### `solveEdges`

```ts
solveEdges(dt: number, iterations: number = 1, substeps: number = 1): this
```

Solve all edge constraints for one substep in XPBD form. A link's `stiff` value is a
geometric knob: it is the fraction of the remaining constraint violation resolved per
update, independent of the particles' masses and of the substep/iteration counts
(per Müller et al. 2007, the per-pass fraction is `1-(1-stiff)^(1/passes)`), and
`stiff=1` is a rigid projection. Mapping the fraction to a mass-relative compliance
keeps a heavy body exactly as stiff as a light one at the same value.
This is the solver used internally by [`World.update`](#physics-world-update);
[`Body.processEdges`](#physics-body-process-edges) remains the simpler relaxation for direct use.

**Parameters**

- `dt` (`number`) — substep time in seconds (reserved; the geometric stiffness does not depend on it)
- `iterations` (`number`; default `1`) — solver iterations for this substep. Default is 1.
- `substeps` (`number`; default `1`) — the caller's substeps per update, for pass-count-independent stiffness. Default is 1.

<a id="physics-body-static-from-group"></a>
##### `fromGroup`

*static*

```ts
static fromGroup(body: PtIterable, stiff: number = 1, autoLink: boolean = true, autoMass: boolean = true): Body
```

Create and populate a body.

**Parameters**

- `body` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> to define the body
- `stiff` (`number`; default `1`) — stiffness value from 0 to 1, where 1 is the most stiff. Default is 1.
- `autoLink` (`boolean`; default `true`) — Automatically create links between the Pts. This usually works for regular convex polygons. Default is true.
- `autoMass` (`boolean`; default `true`) — Automatically calculate the mass based on the area of the polygon. Default is true.

<a id="physics-world"></a>
### `World`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Physics.ts:13`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Physics.ts#L13)

A `World` stores and manages [`Body`](#physics-body) and [`Particle`](#physics-particle) for 2D physics simulation.
It advances with a substepped position-based (XPBD-style) solver and a spatial-hash broad phase.
See a [Particle demo](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=physics.particles) and a [Body demo](https://ptsjs.org/demo/index.html?name=physics.shapes) on the demo page.

#### Constructors

<a id="physics-world-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new World(bound: PtIterable, friction: number = 1, gravity: number | PtLike = 0): World
```

Create a `World` for 2D physics simulation.

**Parameters**

- `bound` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> representing a rectangular bounding box
- `friction` (`number`; default `1`) — a value between 0 to 1, where 1 means no friction. Default is 1
- `gravity` (`number | PtLike`; default `0`) — a number of a Pt to define gravitational force. A number is a shorthand to set `new Pt(0, n)`. Default is 0.

#### Accessors


```ts
set bound(bound: Bound): void
```

Current bound in this `World`.

##### `damping`

```ts
set damping(f: number): void
```

Current damping in this `World`.


Current friction in this `World`.

##### `gravity`

```ts
get gravity(): Pt
set gravity(g: Pt): void
```

Current gravity in this `World`.

<a id="physics-world-iterations"></a>
##### `iterations`

```ts
get iterations(): number
set iterations(f: number): void
```

Constraint solver iterations per substep.

<a id="physics-world-max-time-step"></a>
##### `maxTimeStep`

```ts
get maxTimeStep(): number
set maxTimeStep(ms: number): void
```

Maximum simulated time in milliseconds per [`World.update`](#physics-world-update) call. Larger elapsed
times are clamped so that a hitch (eg, a backgrounded tab) cannot destabilize the
simulation. Default is 50.

<a id="physics-world-particle-count"></a>
##### `particleCount`

```ts
get particleCount(): number
```

Get the number of particles.

<a id="physics-world-substeps"></a>
##### `substeps`

```ts
get substeps(): number
set substeps(n: number): void
```

Number of solver substeps per [`World.update`](#physics-world-update) call. More substeps produce a more
stable and accurate simulation at a linear cost. Default is 4.

<a id="physics-world-integrate"></a>
##### `integrate`

*protected*

```ts
integrate(p: Particle, dt: number, prevDt: number): Particle
```

Integrate a particle for one substep: Verlet with the accumulated force plus gravity as
acceleration, and the substep-adjusted friction as drag. Forces are read but not cleared
here — they persist across the substeps of one update and are cleared when it completes.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`Particle`) — particle
- `dt` (`number`) — substep time in seconds
- `prevDt` (`number`) — unused; substeps are equal so no time-correction is needed. Kept for signature compatibility.


**Returns:** a Particle, or undefined if not found

```ts
particleIndex(name: string): number
```


**Parameters**

- `count` (`number`; default `1`) — Number of items to remove. Default is 1.

<a id="physics-world-remove-particle"></a>

```ts
removeParticle(from: string | number, count: number = 1): this
```

Remove particles from this world. Support removing a range and negative index.

**Parameters**

- `from` (`string | number`) — Start index, which can be negative (where -1 is at index 0, -2 at index 1, etc)
- `count` (`number`; default `1`) — Number of items to remove. Default is 1.

<a id="physics-world-update"></a>
##### `update`

```ts
update(ms: number): void
```

Advance this world by an amount of time, solved in [`World.substeps`](#physics-world-substeps) substeps.
The time is clamped to [`World.maxTimeStep`](#physics-world-max-time-step). Draw callbacks fire once per call,
after the solve completes.

**Parameters**

- `ms` (`number`) — change in time in milliseconds

*static*

```ts
static boundConstraint(p: Particle, rect: PtIterable, damping: number = 0.75): void
```

Static function to calculate bounding box constraints.

**Parameters**

- `p` (`Particle`) — particle
- `rect` (`PtIterable`) — a Group or an Iterable<Pt> representing a bounding box
- `damping` (`number`; default `0.75`) — damping between 0 to 1, where 1 means no damping. Default is 0.75.

<a id="physics-world-static-edge-constraint"></a>
##### `edgeConstraint`

*static*

```ts
static edgeConstraint(p1: Particle, p2: Particle, dist: number, stiff: number = 1, precise: boolean = false): Particle
```

Static function to calculate edge constraints between 2 particles.

**Parameters**

- `p1` (`Particle`) — particle 1
- `p2` (`Particle`) — particle 1
- `dist` (`number`) — distance between particles
- `stiff` (`number`; default `1`) — stiffness between 0 to 1.
- `precise` (`boolean`; default `false`) — use precise distance calculation. Default is `false`.

<a id="module-play"></a>
## Module: `Play`

<a id="play-sound"></a>
### `Sound`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Play.ts:195`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Play.ts#L195)

Sound class simplifies common tasks like audio inputs and visualizations using a subset of Web Audio API. It can be used with other audio libraries like tone.js, and extended to support additional web audio functions. See [the guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Sound-0800.html) to get started.

#### Constructors

<a id="play-sound-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new Sound(type: SoundType, ctx: AudioContext): Sound
```

Construct a `Sound` instance. Usually, it's more convenient to use one of the static methods like [`Sound.load`](#play-sound-static-load) or [`Sound.from`](#play-sound-static-from).
By default, all instances share a single `AudioContext` (browsers limit how many can be live at once).

**Parameters**

- `type` (`SoundType`) — a `SoundType` string: "file", "input", or "gen"
- `ctx` (`AudioContext`) — Optionally provide your own AudioContext instead of the shared one

#### Accessors

<a id="play-sound-bin-size"></a>


If an analyzer is added (see [`analyze`](#play-sound-analyze) function), get the number of frequency bins in the analyzer. Returns 0 if no analyzer is added.

##### `ctx`

```ts
get ctx(): AudioContext
```

Get this Sound's AudioContext instance for advanced use-cases.


If the sound is generated, this sets and gets the frequency of the tone.


Get this Sound's AudioNode subclass instance for advanced use-cases.


Get this Sound's Output node AudioNode instance for advanced use-cases.

##### `playable`


Indicate whether the sound is ready to play. When loading from a file, this corresponds to a ["canplaythrough"](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/readyState) event.
You can also use `this.source.addEventListener( 'canplaythrough', ...)` if needed. See also [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLMediaElement/canplaythrough_event).

##### `playing`


Indicate whether the sound is currently playing.

A value between 0 to 1 to indicate playback progress. Returns 0 if the sound has no duration (eg, generated or input sounds).



Get this Sound's Audio element (if used) instance for advanced use-cases. See [`Sound.load`](#play-sound-static-load).


Get this Sound's MediaStream (eg, from microphone, if in use) instance for advanced use-cases. See [`Sound.input`](#play-sound-static-input)

##### `type`

```ts

```

Get the type of input for this Sound instance. Either "file", "input", or "gen"

##### `volume`

```ts
get volume(): number

```

Get and set the volume of this sound. Default is 1. Values above 1 amplify the sound. Can be set before or during playback.

#### Methods

<a id="play-sound-analyze"></a>
##### `analyze`

```ts
analyze(size: number = 256, minDb: number = -100, maxDb: number = -30, smooth: number = 0.8): this
```

Add an analyzer to this `Sound`. Calling it again replaces the existing analyzer.

**Parameters**

- `size` (`number`; default `256`) — the number of frequency bins. Should be a power of 2.
- `minDb` (`number`; default `-100`) — Optional minimum decibels (corresponds to `AnalyserNode.minDecibels`)
- `maxDb` (`number`; default `-30`) — Optional maximum decibels (corresponds to `AnalyserNode.maxDecibels`)
- `smooth` (`number`; default `0.8`) — Optional smoothing value (corresponds to `AnalyserNode.smoothingTimeConstant`)

<a id="play-sound-connect"></a>
##### `connect`

```ts
connect(node: AudioNode): this
```

Connect another AudioNode to this `Sound` instance's AudioNode. Using this function, you can extend the capabilities of this `Sound` instance for advanced use cases such as filtering. The connection is restored if a generated sound is restarted.

**Parameters**

- `node` (`AudioNode`) — another AudioNode

<a id="play-sound-create-buffer"></a>
##### `createBuffer`

```ts
createBuffer(buf: AudioBuffer): this
```

Create or re-use an AudioBuffer. Only needed if you are using `Sound.loadAsBuffer` and want to prepare a replay manually — [`start`](#play-sound-start) re-creates a used buffer automatically.

**Parameters**

- `buf` (`AudioBuffer`) — an AudioBuffer. Optionally, you can call this without parameters to re-use existing buffer.

<a id="play-sound-dispose"></a>
##### `dispose`

```ts
dispose(): this
```

Stop playing and disconnect all nodes (including analyzer and volume), and release stream, source, and buffer references.
The instance should not be used after calling this. Note that this never closes an `AudioContext`: the shared context lives for the page, and a context you provided is yours to close.

<a id="play-sound-freq-domain"></a>
##### `freqDomain`

```ts
freqDomain(): Uint8Array
```

Get the raw frequency-domain data from analyzer as unsigned 8-bit integers. An analyzer must be added before calling this function (See [analyze](#play-sound-analyze) function).

<a id="play-sound-freq-domain-to"></a>
##### `freqDomainTo`

```ts
freqDomainTo(size: PtLike, position: PtLike = ..., trim: number[] = ..., out: Group): Group
```

Map the frequency-domain data from analyzer to a range. An analyzer must be added before calling this function (See [analyze](#play-sound-analyze) function).

**Parameters**

- `size` (`PtLike`) — map each data point `[index, value]` to `[width, height]`
- `position` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — Optionally, set a starting `[x, y]` position. Default is `[0, 0]`
- `trim` (`number[]`; default `...`) — Optionally, trim the start and end values by `[startTrim, data.length-endTrim]`
- `out` (`Group`) — Optionally, provide a `Group` (usually one returned by a previous call) whose Pts will be reused instead of allocating new ones — recommended when calling once per frame

**Returns:** a Group containing the mapped values

**Example**

```ts
form.point( s.freqDomainTo( space.size ) )
```

<a id="play-sound-remove-output-node"></a>
##### `removeOutputNode`

```ts
removeOutputNode(): this
```

Removes the 'output' node added from setOutputNode
Note: if you start the Sound after calling this, it will play via the default node

##### `reset`

```ts
reset(): this
```

Stop playing and disconnect the AudioNode.

<a id="play-sound-set-output-node"></a>
##### `setOutputNode`


Sets the 'output' node for this Sound
This would typically be used after Sound.connect, if you are adding nodes
in your chain for filtering purposes.

##### `start`

```ts

```

Start playing. Internally this connects the `AudioNode` to `AudioContext`'s destination.
Calling `start( timeAt )` while a file or buffer sound is playing seeks to that time; a generated sound that is already playing is unaffected.

**Parameters**

- `timeAt` (`number`; default `0`) — optional parameter to play from a specific time, in seconds

<a id="play-sound-stop"></a>
##### `stop`

```ts
stop(): this
```

Stop playing. Internally this also disconnects the `AudioNode` from `AudioContext`'s destination. Calling `stop` when the sound is not playing has no effect.

<a id="play-sound-time-domain"></a>
##### `timeDomain`

```ts
timeDomain(): Uint8Array
```

Get the raw time-domain data from analyzer as unsigned 8-bit integers. An analyzer must be added before calling this function (See [analyze](#play-sound-analyze) function).

<a id="play-sound-time-domain-to"></a>
##### `timeDomainTo`

```ts
timeDomainTo(size: PtLike, position: PtLike = ..., trim: number[] = ..., out: Group): Group
```

Map the time-domain data from analyzer to a range. An analyzer must be added before calling this function (See [analyze](#play-sound-analyze) function).

**Parameters**

- `size` (`PtLike`) — map each data point `[index, value]` to `[width, height]`
- `position` (`PtLike`; default `...`) — Optionally, set a starting `[x, y]` position. Default is `[0, 0]`
- `trim` (`number[]`; default `...`) — Optionally, trim the start and end values by `[startTrim, data.length-endTrim]`
- `out` (`Group`) — Optionally, provide a `Group` (usually one returned by a previous call) whose Pts will be reused instead of allocating new ones — recommended when calling once per frame

**Returns:** a Group containing the mapped values

**Example**

```ts
form.point( s.timeDomainTo( space.size ) )
```

<a id="play-sound-toggle"></a>
##### `toggle`

```ts
toggle(): this
```

Toggle between `start` and `stop`.

<a id="play-sound-static-from"></a>
##### `from`

*static*

```ts
static from(node: AudioNode, ctx: AudioContext, type: SoundType = "gen", stream: MediaStream): Sound
```

Create a `Sound` given an [AudioNode](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioNode) and an [AudioContext](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AudioContext) from Web Audio API. See also [this example](https://ptsjs.org/guide/js/examples/tone.html) using tone.js in the [guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Sound-0800.html).

**Parameters**

- `node` (`AudioNode`) — an AudioNode instance
- `ctx` (`AudioContext`) — an AudioContext instance
- `type` (`SoundType`; default `"gen"`) — a string representing a type of input source: either "file", "input", or "gen".
- `stream` (`MediaStream`) — Optionally include a MediaStream, if the type is "input"

**Returns:** a `Sound` instance

<a id="play-sound-static-generate"></a>
##### `generate`

*static*

```ts
static generate(type: OscillatorType, val: number | PeriodicWave): Sound
```

Create a `Sound` by generating a waveform using [OscillatorNode](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/OscillatorNode).

**Parameters**

- `type` (`OscillatorType`) — a string representing the waveform type: "sine", "square", "sawtooth", "triangle", "custom"
- `val` (`number | PeriodicWave`) — the frequency value in Hz to play, or a PeriodicWave instance if type is "custom".

**Returns:** a `Sound` instance

**Example**

```ts
Sound.generate( 'sine', 120 )
```

<a id="play-sound-static-input"></a>
##### `input`

*static*

```ts
static input(constraint: MediaStreamConstraints): Promise
```

Create a `Sound` by streaming from an input device like microphone. Note that this function returns a Promise which resolves to a Sound instance, and rejects if the input device is unavailable or permission is denied.

**Parameters**

- `constraint` (`MediaStreamConstraints`) — Optional constraints which can be used to select a specific input device. For example, you may use [`enumerateDevices`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/enumerateDevices) to find a specific deviceId;

**Returns:** a `Promise` which resolves to `Sound` instance

**Example**

```ts
Sound.input().then( s => sound = s ).catch( err => ... );
```

<a id="play-sound-static-load"></a>
##### `load`

*static*

```ts
static load(source: string | HTMLMediaElement, crossOrigin: string = "anonymous"): Promise
```

Create a `Sound` by loading from a sound file or an audio element.

**Parameters**

- `source` (`string | HTMLMediaElement`) — either an url string to load a sound file, or an audio element.
- `crossOrigin` (`string`; default `"anonymous"`) — whether to support loading cross-origin. Default is "anonymous". When passing an audio element, set the attribute in markup before the element loads for it to take effect.

**Returns:** a `Sound` instance

**Example**

```ts
Sound.load( '/path/to/file.mp3' )
```

<a id="play-sound-static-load-as-buffer"></a>
##### `loadAsBuffer`

*static*

```ts
static loadAsBuffer(url: string): Promise
```

Create a `Sound` by loading from a sound file url as `AudioBufferSourceNode`.
Use this method for now if you need to visualize sound in Safari and iOS. Once Apple has full support for FFT with streaming `HTMLMediaElement`, this method will likely be deprecated.

**Parameters**

- `url` (`string`) — an url to the sound file

Analyzer if any


<a id="play-tempo-every"></a>
##### `every`

```ts
every(beats: number | number[]): ITempoResponses
```

This is a core function that let you specify a rhythm and then define responses by calling the `start` and `progress` functions from the returned object. See [Animation guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Animation-0700.html) for more details.
The `start` function lets you set a callback on every start. It takes a function ([`ITempoStartFn`](#types-itempostartfn)).
The `progress` function lets you set a callback during progress. It takes a function ([`ITempoProgressFn`](#types-itempoprogressfn)). Both functions let you optionally specify a time offset and a custom name.
A positive offset shifts the beat earlier (fires sooner), a negative offset shifts it later.

**Parameters**

- `beats` (`number | number[]`) — a rhythm in beats as a number or an array of numbers

**Returns:** an object with chainable functions

**Example**

```ts
tempo.every(2).start( (count) => ... )`, `tempo.every([2,4,6]).progress( (count, t) => ... )
```

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Pt.ts:1010`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L1010)

### `Group`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Pt.ts:559`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L559)

##### `$matrixAdd`

```ts
$matrixAdd(g: number | GroupLike | number[][]): Group
```

Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix addition.

<a id="pt-group-dollar-matrix-multiply"></a>
##### `$matrixMultiply`

```ts
$matrixMultiply(g: number | GroupLike, transposed: boolean = false, elementwise: boolean = false): Group
```

Apply this group as a matrix and calculate matrix multiplication.

**Parameters**

- `g` (`number | GroupLike`) — a scalar number, an array of numeric arrays, or a Group of K Pts, each with N dimensions (K-rows, N-columns) -- or if transposed is true, then N Pts with K dimensions
- `transposed` (`boolean`; default `false`) — (Only applicable if it's not elementwise multiplication) If true, then a and b's columns should match (ie, each Pt should have the same dimensions). Default is `false`.
- `elementwise` (`boolean`; default `false`) — if true, then the multiplication is done element-wise. Default is `false`.

**Returns:** If not elementwise, this will return a new  Group with M Pt, each with N dimensions (M-rows, N-columns).

<a id="pt-group-dollar-zip"></a>
##### `$zip`

```ts
$zip(defaultValue: number | boolean = undefined, useLongest: boolean = false): Group
```

Zip a group of Pt. eg, [[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]] => [[1,3,5],[2,4,6]].

**Parameters**

- `defaultValue` (`number | boolean`; default `undefined`) — a default value to fill if index out of bound. If not provided, it will throw an error instead.
- `useLongest` (`boolean`; default `false`) — If true, find the longest list of values in a Pt and use its length for zipping. Default is false, which uses the first item's length for zipping.

<a id="pt-pt"></a>
### `Pt`

**Kind:** Class · **Source:** [`src/Pt.ts:12`](https://github.com/williamngan/pts/blob/master/src/Pt.ts#L12)

**Extends:** `Float32Array`

**Implements:** `IPt`, `Iterable`

Pt is a subclass of standard [`Float32Array`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Float32Array) with additional properties and functions to support vector and geometric calculations.
See [Pt guide](https://ptsjs.org/guide/Pt-0200.html) for details.

#### Constructors

<a id="pt-pt-constructor"></a>
##### Constructor

```ts
new Pt(args: (number | number[] | IPt | Float32Array)[]): Pt
```

Create a Pt. If no parameter is provided, this will instantiate a Pt with 2 dimensions [0, 0].
Note that `new Pt(3)` will only instantiate Pt with length of 3 (ie, same as `new Float32Array(3)` ). If you need a Pt with 1 dimension of value 3, use `new Pt([3])`.

**Parameters**

- `args` (`(number | number[] | IPt | Float32Array)[]`) — a list of numeric parameters, an array of numbers, or an object with {x,y,z,w} properties

**Example**

```ts
new Pt()`, `new Pt(1,2,3,4,5)`, `new Pt([1,2])`, `new Pt({x:0, y:1})`, `new Pt(pt)
```

<a id="pt-pt-op"></a>
##### `op`


```ts
let myOp = pt.op( fn ); let result = myOp( [1,2,3] );
```

<a id="pt-pt-ops"></a>

```ts
ops(fns:  Fn(p1:PtLike, rest:any[])[]):  Fn(rest:any[])[]
```

**Parameters**

- `fns` (` Fn(p1:PtLike, rest:any[])[]`) — an array of functions for `op`

**Returns:** an array of resulting functions

**Example**

```ts
let myOps = pt.ops([fn1, fn2, fn3]); let results = myOps.map( (op) => op([1,2,3]) );
```
